transcript.text: Hi, I've got a Dyson V15 Detect (SV22) about 4 months old. When I go from the kitchen tiles onto the lounge rug the motor suddenly gets much louder and the battery number drops faster, then it calms down again when I go back on the tiles. Also the screen goes up and down by itself. Is the motor on its way out? It's still under guarantee so I want to report it before it dies completely.

Based on your description, it is highly unlikely that the main digital motor (the one in the handle) is failing. In fact, if the motor were dying, you would typically see a drop in suction power and cleaning performance before or alongside any noise changes, not just a change in volume.

The symptoms you are describing—sudden loudness on carpets/rugs, screen flickering/up-and-down numbers, and faster battery drain—are classic signs of one of two things:

### 1. The Laser Slim Fluffy Head is Working as Designed (Most Likely)
The Dyson V15 Detect’s Laser Slim Fluffy head has a piezoelectric sensor that detects dust particles. When it hits a rug or carpet, the motor automatically increases power to boost suction. This causes:
• A noticeable increase in noise (higher RPM = louder sound).
• Faster battery drain (more power usage).
• The screen may flicker or show fluctuating numbers as the sensor recalibrates between surfaces with different dust densities and textures.

✅ Test: Try running the vacuum on a carpet vs. hard floor in the same room. If it’s louder on the carpet even when there’s no visible dirt, that’s normal behavior for the auto-mode.

### 2. A Blockage or Airflow Restriction (Very Common)
If there’s a partial blockage (e.g., in the wand, hose, or filter), the motor has to work harder to pull air through. When you move onto a rug:
• The suction demand increases.
• The motor strains against the restriction → louder noise.
• Battery drains faster due to higher current draw.
• The screen may glitch if there’s an electrical interference from the struggling motor or a loose connection exacerbated by vibration.

✅ Check:
• Empty the bin completely.
• Remove and wash the filters (pre-motor and post-motor), let them dry for 24 hours, then reinstall.
• Check the wand, hose, and turbine head for obstructions (coins, hair, debris).
• Ensure all connections are clicked in firmly.

### 3. Faulty Battery or Power Delivery Issue (Less Likely but Possible)
If the battery is degraded or has a faulty cell, it may struggle under load (like on carpet), causing voltage drops that can:
• Make the motor sound strained/louder.
• Cause screen flickering or erratic readings.

✅ Test: Run the vacuum on tiles only for 10–15 minutes. If the screen stays stable and noise is consistent, but it only misbehaves on rugs/carpet, this points to either auto-power boost (normal) or a blockage/airflow issue.

### 4. Main Motor Failure (Unlikely at This Stage)
A dying main motor usually presents as:
• Loss of suction.
• A grinding, scraping, or whining noise (not just “louder”).
• The vacuum shutting off unexpectedly due to overheating.
• Error codes on the screen.

---

### Recommended Action Plan:
1. Perform a full maintenance check: Clean filters, empty bin, clear all blockages. Let filters dry 24h if washed.
2. Test in auto-mode vs. max mode: Try running on carpet in Max mode (manual). If it’s still abnormally loud and the screen flickers, note this for Dyson.
3. Monitor suction: Is cleaning performance actually worse on rugs? If yes, it’s likely a blockage or filter issue.
4. Contact Dyson Support: Since it’s under warranty, report the issue. Mention:
• The noise increase and battery drain on carpets.
• The screen flickering/up-and-down numbers.
• That you’ve already checked for blockages and cleaned filters.

Dyson often replaces entire units (including head, wand, and bin) if they suspect a fault, so it’s worth raising the ticket now before any potential failure escalates. They may ask you to return the vacuum for inspection or send a replacement part.

Bottom line: Don’t panic—it’s likely normal auto-behavior or a simple blockage/filter issue—but yes, report it under warranty now to be safe.

Yes, this changes things significantly! Since you have the Digital Motorbar (not the Laser Slim Fluffy) and the noise/battery drain happens specifically when transitioning to rugs, here’s what’s likely going on:

### Most Likely Cause: Brush Bar Strain or Blockage in the Head
The Digital Motorbar has a motorized brush bar. When you move from hard tiles to a rug:
• The brush bar encounters more resistance (friction) from the rug fibers.
• If there’s hair, string, or debris wrapped around the brush bar ends or bearings, the motor struggles → louder noise + faster battery drain.
• Once back on tiles, resistance drops → motor calms down.

✅ Check this:
1. Turn off and unplug the vacuum.
2. Flip over the Digital Motorbar head.
3. Use a coin to slide open the brush bar compartment.
4. Remove the brush bar and check for:
• Hair or string wrapped around the ends (especially near the bearings).
• Debris stuck in the bearing housings.
5. Spin the brush bar by hand – it should spin freely with no grinding or resistance.

### Secondary Check: Main Motor or Battery Issue?
If the brush bar spins freely and is clean, but the problem persists, consider:
• Battery degradation: A 4-month-old battery shouldn’t be degrading unless there’s a fault. However, if the battery cells are inconsistent under load (rug = higher power draw), voltage may drop temporarily → screen flickers + faster drain.
• Main motor strain: Less likely without burning smell or loss of suction, but possible if bearings in the main motor are failing.

### Recommended Steps:
1. Clean and inspect the Digital Motorbar head thoroughly (as above). This is the #1 culprit for rug-specific noise/battery issues.
2. Test on a different rug/carpet to see if the issue is consistent or specific to one rug type.
3. Check battery health: Dyson’s app (if you use it) may show battery cycles. If not, note how long runtime is on tiles vs. rugs. Significant drop suggests a load-sensitive battery fault.

### Since It’s Under Guarantee:
If cleaning the head doesn’t resolve it, contact Dyson Support. Mention:
• The vacuum is 4 months old.
• Noise and battery drain spike specifically when transitioning to rugs.
• Screen flickers/fluctuates during this transition.
• No loss of suction or burning smell.

They may offer a replacement head, battery, or full unit repair/replacement under warranty. Don’t wait for it to "die completely" – report it now while you’re within the guarantee period.
